=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh
  Line or code reference: 78-83 (restore origin validation) and 85-93 (restore extraheader validation)
  Problem: Restore checks only that origin matches `^https://github.com/` (line 81) without verifying the path component against GITHUB_REPOSITORY or a trusted-support checkout. An editor-changed origin like `https://github.com/attacker/repo.git` passes this check and receives GH_TOKEN injected into the URL. The restore path also processes extraheader entries (lines 85-93) without validating the repo-scoped path against the verified origin or checking that the same repo had a validated origin entry first. Both `test_restore_does_not_send_token_to_an_editor_changed_origin` and `test_restore_rejects_marker_header_without_a_validated_origin` (added in LAST RUN DIFF) fail in CI.
  Why it fails at runtime: The editor process can change origin to any github.com URL, and restore will inject the workflow's GH_TOKEN into it. An extraheader marker entry without a corresponding origin entry also receives the credential header.
  Severity: BLOCKER; confidence: 5.
- File: scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh
  Line or code reference: 21-27, 55-59, 98-102
  Problem: Every exit path in the script returns 0 unconditionally. Line 102 is `exit 0`. Lines 23, 27, 56, and 59 also exit 0 on error conditions. The `failed` variable is set to true on origin mismatch (line 83), extraheader rejection (line 88, 92), unexpected marker items (line 94), pushurl validation gaps, and other failure paths, but is never used to determine the exit status. Line 98 only uses `failed` to decide whether to truncate the marker file, not to exit non-zero.
  Why it fails at runtime: All 15 CI tests in tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py that assert `returncode != 0` fail because the script always exits 0. Workflow callers that invoke this script via `trap` (implement.yml line 2730) and explicit restore calls cannot detect credential-hiding or credential-restoration failures. The editor launches with credentials still present or proceeds without them being safely restored.
  Severity: BLOCKER; confidence: 5.
- File: scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh
  Line or code reference: 29-54 (hide function body)
  Problem: The hide function strips credentials from remote.origin.url and extraheader git config keys, but does not inspect or clear remote.origin.pushurl or url.*.pushInsteadOf rewrite rules. Tests `test_hide_rejects_an_explicit_push_url_before_editor_launch` and `test_hide_rejects_preexisting_push_url_rewrite` expect hide to reject checkouts with pre-existing pushurl or pushInsteadOf, but the script only processes origin url and extraheaders.
  Why it fails at runtime: A pre-configured pushurl remains in .git/config after hide runs. The editor process can still push to the pushurl destination that may contain credentials or point to an attacker-controlled repository. CI confirms the test assertions fail because hide exits 0 without rejecting.
  Severity: BLOCKER; confidence: 5.
- File: scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh
  Line or code reference: 62-97 (restore loop)
  Problem: The restore loop processes marker entries sequentially and injects tokens as it iterates. It does not pre-validate all checkouts before injecting any token. `test_restore_validates_every_checkout_before_injecting_any_token` expects that when one checkout fails validation (e.g. editor-changed origin), no other checkout receives credentials. The script currently injects into the first checkout before discovering the second checkout is invalid.
  Why it fails at runtime: If the editor changes one checkout's origin to an attacker URL, restore first writes GH_TOKEN into the valid repo checkout, then detects the bad one. The editor can then use the injected credentials from the valid checkout even though the overall restore should have been rejected. CI confirms the test fails with exit 0.
  Severity: BLOCKER; confidence: 5.

  Line or code reference: 29
